opportunities.title: Apprenticeships Suppliers Framework
opportunities.description: West Sussex County Council are creating a new Flexible Framework for Apprenticeships to onboard training delivery providers. This framework is intended to establish a flexible and high-quality pool of approved Apprenticeship Suppliers who can deliver a broad range of services across defined Lots: Lot 1 Health & Social Care Lot 2 Education, Early Years & Community Support Lot 3 Business, Administration & Management Lot 4 Digital, Technology & Data Lot 5 Creative, Cultural, Media, Marketing & Design Lot 6 Engineering, Construction, Built Environment, Transport, Environment & Sustainability Lot 7 Public Services, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, Protective Services & Community Safety The total contract value is £50 million, this has been split between all lots as an estimate not an actual figure. Please note that this Framework will remain open to applicants for the full life time of this Framework. Call off competitions will commence in 2027.

lots.title: Health & Social Care
lots.description: This lot covers apprenticeships that develop skills for roles across health, clinical support, adult social care, children’s care, and community wellbeing. It includes, but is not limited to, standards supporting public health, social work support, and wider care services.

lots.title: Education, Early Years & Community Support
lots.description: This lot includes apprenticeships for professionals working in schools, early years settings, and wider community learning and support environments. It covers teaching assistants, early years practitioners, youth work, learning mentors, SEND support, and careers guidance. It also includes community-focused roles that support wellbeing, education engagement, family support, outreach, coaching, and local community development activities.

lots.title: Business, Administration & Management
lots.description: This lot covers apprenticeships supporting core business operations and organisational effectiveness. It includes, but is not limited to, business administration, human resources, project and programme management, leadership and management, and business improvement roles. This lot focuses on developing strong operational, organisational, and managerial capability.

lots.title: Digital, Technology & Data
lots.description: This lot includes digital and IT apprenticeships that strengthen organisational technology capability. It covers, but is not limited to, software development, cyber security, data and AI roles, digital support, cloud and infrastructure operations, and digital transformation functions.

lots.title: Creative, Cultural, Media, Marketing & Design
lots.description: This lot covers apprenticeships across the creative industries, cultural sectors, marketing, media and communications, and design professions. It includes, but is not limited to, content and creative production, digital and graphic design, cultural heritage, marketing and digital marketing, communications, and design led roles. This lot supports creative, promotional, and content driven capability across sectors.

lots.title: Engineering, Construction, Transport, Environment Built & Sustainability
lots.description: This lot covers technical and professional apprenticeships across engineering disciplines, the built environment, transport operations, and environmental or sustainability focused roles. It includes, but is not limited to, engineering; construction and building services; and surveying roles. It also incorporates transport focused pathways such as transport planning and infrastructure support, alongside roles related to environmental management and sustainability practices.

lots.title: Public Services, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, Protective Services, CommunityS
lots.description: This lot covers apprenticeships supporting public protection, statutory duties, legal and regulatory functions, commercial governance, and community safety. It includes, but is not limited to, fire and rescue, legal services, compliance, regulatory affairs, and commercial procurement roles. It also incorporates community facing protective services such as community safety officers and anti social behaviour teams.

opportunities.description: The Connect to Work (Connect to Work - GOV.UK) programme is a Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) funded initiative designed to support individuals who are economically inactive or at risk of leaving employment to access and sustain suitable work. The programme forms part of the Government's Get Britain Working strategy, which aims to reduce economic inactivity and support more people into good, sustainable employment through locally led and integrated approaches. The purpose of this procurement is to appoint one or more Delivery Partners to deliver supported employment services as part of the Connect to Work programme in Somerset. The programme will support: • individuals who are economically inactive and wish to work; and • individuals who are in work but at risk of falling out of employment Support will be delivered using the following evidence-based supported employment models that form separate Lots: • Lot 1 - Individual Placement and Support (IPS); and • Lot 2 - Supported Employment Quality Framework (SEQF)

methodology.inclusion: Only procurement records already classified as relevant and publishable by the CareerPath procurement engine are eligible. Active tenders, current pipeline/engagement records and recent awards are retained; stale historical records are excluded.
methodology.requirements: Requirement, commercial and performance signals are deterministic extracts from published notice text. They are not an interpretation of unpublished tender documents and are never presented as complete bid requirements.
methodology.evaluation: Evaluation weightings are displayed only when present in structured public procurement data.
methodology.noPrediction: CareerPath does not publish win-probability scores or undisclosed commercial recommendations in this public feed.
methodology.supplyChain: Supply-chain records are taken from public prime-provider partnership and expression-of-interest pages. CareerPath reports only information explicitly published by the provider and does not infer unpublished selection criteria, commercial terms or win probability.
methodology.programmeLinking: Opportunity-to-programme links use an explicit CareerPath registry. Generic classifications such as Employment Support and IPS are not guessed into a specific programme.
methodology.sourceCoverage: CareerPath publishes source coverage and known gaps explicitly. A missing record is never treated as proof that no opportunity exists.
methodology.supplierIntelligence: Supplier and incumbent intelligence uses only published award/contract supplier names. Market counts describe the curated CareerPath dataset and are not market-share estimates.
methodology.readiness: Published-data readiness flags show which facts are available for an opportunity. They are not rankings, scores, suitability assessments or recommendations.
methodology.recommissioningDelta: CareerPath automatically publishes a derived predecessor comparison only when commissioner, programme, geography, chronology and scope similarity satisfy the strong-match gate. Weaker candidates remain internal for review. Derived matches are not proof of formal lineage unless source material explicitly establishes it.
methodology.workforceSignals: Workforce figures are aggregated returned-vacancy and advertised-salary observations from CareerPath programme intelligence. They are not total market vacancy counts, staffing requirements or evidence that a named provider has won a contract.
methodology.localDeliveryContext: Local indicators are shown only where CareerPath can safely match an opportunity geography to a programme regional series.
